description:
Everything that happened to one stock over the last 90 days, in one timeline,
newest first: news, SEC 8-K filings, insider clusters and large single trades,
earnings dates and reported results, analyst target and rating changes, and
screener setups. Answers "what has been going on
with this stock?" in one call instead of five.

Each item has a `type` (news | filing | insider | earnings | analyst | setup), an
ISO `timestamp`, a plain `headline` and a type-specific `extra` object. With no
`types` the timeline is the "All" view: very weak news is left out and upcoming
earnings within 30 days are returned separately under `upcoming`; with `types` you
get just those kinds, news included in full (for Pro; see below for Free). `counts` is how many items of each kind
exist in the window, whatever the page or filter; with no `types` its sum can exceed `total`, because the
all-types list leaves out very weak news, shows a reported quarter once and lists upcoming dates separately.

What each type is:
- news: an article about the company (third-party reporting; the headline is the
  article's own).
- filing: an SEC 8-K, with its item labels. Earnings coverage that repeats a results
  filing is folded into it (`extra.related_news`). Filings are recorded for US-listed
  companies in USD with a market cap of about $1 billion or more.
- insider: a cluster of 3 or more insiders buying or selling within 30 days, with the
  amount in the headline.
- earnings: a reporting date (`extra.date`, `extra.upcoming`, `extra.estimate`), or a
  reported quarter. Where its EPS can be matched to the analysts' estimate, the headline
  says whether EPS beat, missed or was in line with estimates; Pro's content adds the
  figures. A stock with no estimate data keeps its row as it was.
- analyst: the consensus target or rating moved by 5% or more; consecutive steps in one
  direction are one item.
- setup: a screener setup flagged on the stock (Pro).

Every account gets the facts: all types except setups over the 90 days, with the plain
headline in full and the same page size. Three allowances match the other Free tools: Free
returns the 5 newest articles of the last 30 days (as get_stock_news does; `news_note` says
so), the 5 most recent SEC 8-K filings (as get_stock_filings does; `filings_note` says so),
an analyst item names the direction only, and so does an EPS beat or miss on a reported
quarter (never the estimate or a percentage). Pro adds related news and filings, and these fields:
`tone` (Positive/Negative/Neutral, describing
the news for the company, not a price call), `number` with its `number_label` (a 0-100
score for news and setups, relevance for filings), a short `summary`, the model's own
filing headline, fuller `extra` fields (analyst target and rating levels, insider total value and trades), and the
setup items themselves (everyone else is told only that the stock has some, under
`locked_types`; the number is not sent).

Not the same as get_signals, which is the market-wide queue of freshly screened
ideas across all stocks (Pro, last 24 hours, ranked by signal_score). A setup here is
one such idea for this stock, one item among six kinds in its history. For articles
alone use get_stock_news; for filings alone, get_stock_filings.

If a source could not be read just now, `status` is "partial" and `unavailable` lists the
kinds left out (of those you asked for): an empty list for them does not mean nothing
happened. Call again shortly.
For informational purposes only. Not financial advice.

limit.description: Items per page (default 25, max 50). The whole call counts as one call toward your daily limit.

page.description: Page number, starting at 1. `pages` in the response says how many there are.

symbol.description: Stock ticker symbol. Also accepts a company name as a fallback when it uniquely resolves to one symbol.

types.description: Which kinds of items to return: any of "news", "filing", "insider", "earnings", "analyst", "setup" (default: all). Unknown names are an error that lists the valid ones.
